heading: Practise for the Staatsexamen NT2.
lead: Timed practice papers for the reading, listening and writing parts of the Dutch state exam in Dutch as a second language, for Programma I (B1) and Programma II (B2). Behind them is a complete Dutch course from first words to C1, so you can work on whatever the papers show you are missing.
fineprint: The Dutch course is free. The practice papers are part of Premium, €8.99 a month or €69.99 a year. Also available for German speakers.

sections.heading: What the four parts ask
sections.intro: The College voor Toetsen en Examens (CvTE) is responsible for the exam's content, and DUO runs registration and results. Each programme has four parts (onderdelen), all taken on a computer at an exam location in the Netherlands, and you register for each part separately. Most tasks are about work or study, some about daily life. You do not have to take Programma I before Programma II.
rows: 6 texts, 36 multiple-choice questions, 110 minutes. Texts in a paper booklet, questions on screen.
3 texts with 18 questions, on screen and without a dictionary. 55 minutes for Programma I, 50 for Programma II.
About 40 multiple-choice questions on 5 or more recordings, including 1–3 video clips, 90 minutes. Each recording plays once.
20 questions in 45 minutes, without video clips, one voice per recording.
8 sentence tasks, 2 short message or form tasks and 2 short texts, 100 minutes.
7 or 8 sentence tasks, 1 or 2 short and 1 or 2 medium-length writing tasks, 100 minutes.
Programma I: 6 tasks in 50 minutes. Programma II: 4 sentence tasks, one short and one medium-length task in 55 minutes. Rated by AI.
8 short and 8 medium tasks answered into a microphone, about 25 minutes.
4 short, 8 medium and 1 long task of two minutes, about 25 minutes.
Not included: Glossa cannot assess free answers yet.
sections.note: Based on the descriptions on staatsexamensnt2.nl and duo.nl, checked in October 2026. The only aid allowed is the paper Van Dale pocket dictionary for Dutch as a second language, in reading and writing.

sections.heading: How a part is passed
sections.intro: Reading and listening are scored by computer, writing and speaking by two trained raters. The raw points of each part are converted into a scale score, and a part passes at a scale score of 500.
items: Each part passes on its own. You get a certificate for each part you pass and can retake a part you failed.
The diploma follows once all four parts are passed. Certificates and the diploma do not expire.
The conversion is not published, so there is no raw pass mark to practise against.

sections.heading: Which programme you need
items: Programma I meets the B1 language requirement for inburgering and for naturalisation, and shows enough Dutch to work or study at mbo level 3 or 4.
Programma II shows enough Dutch to work or study at hbo or university level.
Under the Wet inburgering 2021, the language part of the B1 route is Programma I or Programma II, whichever your municipality's Plan Inburgering en Participatie names.
The authorities that decide on inburgering and naturalisation set the other conditions, so check what applies to you with them.

sections.heading: Papers to practise on, and a course to learn from

items.title: Two papers for each programme
items.text: Original texts and recordings in the exam's task formats, mostly about work and study: internships, job interviews, working from home, safety at work.

items.title: Writing rated by AI
items.text: Your texts are rated by AI, in Programma II on whether each task is done, how understandable the text is, grammar, spelling, word choice, coherence and structure. It is an estimate, not the mark of two raters.

items.title: A full course behind the papers
items.text: 76 modules in eight tiers from A1 to C1, with word order, er, verb clusters and the passive explained directly, so a weak spot in a paper has a module to go back to.

items.title: Feedback that says why
items.text: Every answer in the course gets feedback with a reason and a link to the grammar rule. Every Dutch word can be tapped for its forms, meaning and audio.

sections.heading: How the practice papers differ from the real exam
items: No pass mark. A section's result is the share of its points. The board publishes no conversion into scale scores, so a paper cannot tell you whether you would reach 500.
Shorter than the real parts, in the same task types: about half the tasks, with the time cut to match.
There is no speaking section. Pronunciation practice (Premium) trains how you say things, not the exam's free answers.
Reading is on screen and no dictionary is offered.

Recordings can be replayed, and there are no video clips. In the exam you read the question first and hear the recording once, so do the same here. In Programma II papers each recording has four questions instead of one.
One voice per recording. In conversations all speakers are read by one voice, with their names.
The word ranges in the writing tasks are Glossa's guide; the board publishes no word limits.

items.question: Is Glossa an official NT2 preparation course?
items.answer: No. Glossa is not connected with the CvTE or DUO. The papers follow the published descriptions of the exam, with original content. The CvTE's own practice environment (oefenexamens) on staatsexamensnt2.nl shows the current format.

items.question: Programma I or Programma II?
items.answer: Programma I is at B1 and Programma II at B2. For inburgering, your municipality's plan names which one you take. The authorities that decide on inburgering and naturalisation set the other conditions.

items.question: What is free?
items.answer: The whole Dutch course from A1 to C1, the grammar reference, word practice and the placement test are free. The NT2 practice papers, conversation practice, stories and the other extras are part of Premium.

items.question: Does Glossa prepare me for the speaking part?
items.answer: Not with a practice paper. The course's speaking exercises give pronunciation feedback, and the conversation practice in Premium is practice in answering freely, but neither is rated like the exam.

items.question: I speak German. Is there a course for me?
items.answer: Yes. Dutch for German speakers has the same NT2 papers, with the instructions and explanations in German: NT2 auf Deutsch.

closing.heading: Start with the course, practise with the papers.
closing.text: Sign in with Google, take the placement test if you already know some Dutch, and open the first module or the NT2 papers.
